 ORDER
This is the second repeat bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 filed on behalf of the applicant for grant of bail.
His earlier bail application was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to renew his prayer at an appropriate stage.

The applicant is in custody since 12.06.2022 in connection with Crime No.329/2022 registered at Police Station Kannod, District Dewas (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under sections 363, 366, 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code of 1860 read with Section 5l and 6 of POCSO Act.

sentences.text: As per prosecution story, on 19.05.2022 at about 2:00 to 3:00 AM present applicant on the pretext of marriage abducted the minor prosecutrix took her with him to nearest forest, kept her there for 15 days and committed rape upon her.
Accordingly, offence has been registered against the applicant.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is an innocent person and he has been falsely implicated in this offence.
He is in custody since 12.06.2022.
Investigation is over and charge-sheet has been filed.
Prosecutrix (PW-1) has been examined before the trial Court, she has turned hostile and she has not stated anything about the commission of rape by the present applicant.
Her father Heeralal (PW-4) also turned hostile.
Applicant is permanent resident of Dewas district.
Final conclusion of the trial is likely to take sufficient long time.
Hence, he prays that applicant be enlarged on bail.

Per contra, learned counsel for the objector opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection by submitting that prosecutrix (PW-1) admits that she lived with the present applicant for a period of 15 days in the forest and her mother/complainant (PW-3) has supported that prosecutrix told her that applicant has committed rape upon her.
Therefore, present applicant does not deserve for bail.
Learned counsel for the respondent/ State also opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection.
Perused the impugned order of the trial Court as well as the case diary.

After considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, nature and gravity of offence, arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant and also taking note of the fact that prosecutrix (PW-1) has categorically stated in her statement that present applicant neither abducted nor committed rape upon her, her father (PW-4) also deposed in the same manner; although mother of the prosecutrix (PW-3)
deposed against the present applicant, but her statement was not supported by the prosecutrix and final conclusion of the trial will take sufficient long time.
In view of prima facie evidence available on record, without commenting on the merits of the case, I deem it proper to release the applicant on bail.
Therefore, the application is allowed.

It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.75,000/- (Rupees Seventy Five Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court, as and when required.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) Cr.P.C.
Certified copy as per rules.
(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE Anushree Praveen @ Pappu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125636195/
